content: The term ins and outs refers to fluid balance, where outs (fluid losses) are greater than ins (fluid intake). When fluid losses significantly exceed intake, it can lead to dehydration. Signs of dehydration include increased thirst. In infants, specific signs such as a depressed fontanelle (the soft spot on the head) and cold skin may be observed. In cases of severe dehydration accompanied by shock, a child will exhibit all three critical clinical signs: Children presenting with these signs should be managed urgently using the shock treatment algorithm.
